findings.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:74 — [100/P1] `const uniqueGuests = guests.filter((guest) => !booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email) && !blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest))` does not deduplicate repeated new addresses, so a direct RPC request with the same valid address twice sends duplicate rows to `createMany` and creates duplicate attendees for one booking.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:158 — [100/P1] `const credentials = await getUsersCredentials(ctx.user);` constructs `EventManager` from the attendee caller's credentials even though the mutation writes the booking organizer's event, so an attendee-authorized addition updates the attendee's integrations instead of the organizer's calendar and leaves the authoritative calendar stale.

packages/emails/email-manager.ts:525 — [P1, confidence 100] The guest-add notification path unconditionally sends both host and attendee mail (`emailsToSend.push(sendEmail(() => new OrganizerAddGuestsEmail({ calEvent: calendarEvent })));` and `...calendarEvent.attendees.map(...)`) without receiving or checking `disableStandardEmails.all.host` / `disableStandardEmails.all.attendee`, so event types that explicitly disable standard confirmation email still notify every recipient when a guest is added.

packages/emails/email-manager.ts:541 — [P1, confidence 100] The notification path passes the unsanitized calendar event to both email variants (`new AttendeeScheduledEmail(calendarEvent, attendee)` / `new AttendeeAddGuestsEmail(calendarEvent, attendee)`) instead of the existing `hideCalendarNotes` redaction used by scheduled mail, so adding a guest exposes additional notes in emails despite the event's hide-notes privacy setting.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:22 — [P2, confidence 100] The new guest-management mutation (`export const addGuestsHandler = async ({ ctx, input }: AddGuestsOptions) => {`) has no diff-scoped verification for authorization, duplicate/blacklist filtering, calendar propagation, or recipient-specific notifications, so regressions in the newly introduced booking mutation ship without any acceptance check detecting them.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:167 — `try { await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests); } catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }` suppresses every notification failure and then returns success, so organizers and attendees receive no update while the requester is told guests were added. [P1; confidence 100]

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:92 — `const bookingAttendees = await prisma.booking.update({` persists the new attendees before `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`, so a calendar-provider failure returns an error after the guest list has changed and a retry is rejected because every requested address already exists. [P1; confidence 100]

packages/emails/email-manager.ts:549 — `await Promise.all(emailsToSend);` starts one outbound email operation for every unbounded attendee and submitted guest in a single batch, exhausting SMTP/worker capacity on a large booking after its new guests have already been persisted. [P1; confidence 100]

packages/emails/templates/organizer-add-guests-email.ts:25 — `replyTo: [this.calEvent.organizer.email, ...this.calEvent.attendees.map(({ email }) => email)],` grows the Reply-To header without a bound until mail providers reject it for a large booking, and the handler swallows that rejection while reporting success. [P1; confidence 75]

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:52 — `const isAttendee = !!booking.attendees.find((attendee) => attendee.email === user.email);` grants any existing attendee authority through the line-54 authorization check to append arbitrary third-party email addresses to the booking and trigger calendar/email changes, enabling an invitee to alter an organizer-owned event without organizer or team authorization. [confidence: 75] [severity: P1]

goldens.comment: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.

The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.

The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.

uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
Starting with an array containing an empty string may cause validation issues. Consider starting with an empty array [] and handling the empty state in the MultiEmail component instead.

The `sendAddGuestsEmails` function does not check the `disableStandardEmails` flags in the `EventType` metadata, which may result in sending emails to hosts/attendees even when standard emails are disabled for the event type.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:158 — [100/P1] `const credentials = await getUsersCredentials(ctx.user);` constructs `EventManager` from the attendee caller's credentials even though the mutation writes the booking organizer's event, so an attendee-authorized addition updates the attendee's integrations instead of the organizer's calendar and leaves the authoritative calendar stale.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that in addGuests.handler.ts line 158, `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` gets the credentials of the current user (ctx.user - who could be an attendee or team admin), not the booking organizer. The EventManager is then constructed with these credentials and used to call `updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`. When an attendee adds guests (which is allowed per the permission check on lines 47-51), the calendar update would use the attendee's credentials instead of the organizer's credentials, potentially updating the wrong calendar or failing if the attendee doesn't have calendar integrations. The booking organizer's credentials are available via `booking.user.credentials` (included in the query on line 38) but are not used.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:167 — `try { await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests); } catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }` suppresses every notification failure and then returns success, so organizers and attendees receive no update while the requester is told guests were added. [P1; confidence 100]

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows at lines 167-170 in addGuests.handler.ts that email sending failures are caught and only logged with console.log, then the function returns success with { message: 'Guests added' }. This means if sendAddGuestsEmails fails, the guests are added to the database but no notifications are sent, yet the user sees a success message. This is a real defect - silent failure of a critical notification feature while reporting success to the user.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:92 — `const bookingAttendees = await prisma.booking.update({` persists the new attendees before `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`, so a calendar-provider failure returns an error after the guest list has changed and a retry is rejected because every requested address already exists. [P1; confidence 100]

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a transactional consistency issue in addGuests.handler.ts. Looking at the diff, the code at line 92 does `await prisma.booking.update({...})` to persist new attendees to the database, then later at line 163 calls `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`. If the calendar update fails, the database already has the new guests persisted. On retry, the uniqueGuests filter at lines 68-72 will filter out all guests since they already exist in booking.attendees, causing the 'emails_must_be_unique_valid' error. This is a real atomicity/consistency bug where partial failure leaves the system in an inconsistent state.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/emails/email-manager.ts:549 — `await Promise.all(emailsToSend);` starts one outbound email operation for every unbounded attendee and submitted guest in a single batch, exhausting SMTP/worker capacity on a large booking after its new guests have already been persisted. [P1; confidence 100]

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims this is a P1 bug that exhausts SMTP/worker capacity, but this is a speculative performance concern, not a verifiable defect. The pattern of using Promise.all for sending emails to attendees is consistent with existing code in the same file (e.g., sendLocationChangeEmails at line 520). The diff shows standard email notification logic that iterates over attendees - this is expected behavior for notifying all participants. There's no evidence this causes actual failures or data loss. The 'unbounded' claim is also misleading since attendees are bounded by the booking's actual attendee list, not arbitrary input.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/emails/templates/organizer-add-guests-email.ts:25 — `replyTo: [this.calEvent.organizer.email, ...this.calEvent.attendees.map(({ email }) => email)],` grows the Reply-To header without a bound until mail providers reject it for a large booking, and the handler swallows that rejection while reporting success. [P1; confidence 75]

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies two real issues in the diff: 1) The Reply-To header in organizer-add-guests-email.ts line 25 includes all attendees without any limit, which could grow unbounded for large bookings. 2) In addGuests.handler.ts lines 170-173, the sendAddGuestsEmails call is wrapped in try/catch that only logs 'Error sending AddGuestsEmails' but the handler still returns success with 'Guests added' message. This means email failures are silently swallowed while reporting success to the user. Both issues are verifiable in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:52 — `const isAttendee = !!booking.attendees.find((attendee) => attendee.email === user.email);` grants any existing attendee authority through the line-54 authorization check to append arbitrary third-party email addresses to the booking and trigger calendar/email changes, enabling an invitee to alter an organizer-owned event without organizer or team authorization. [confidence: 75] [severity: P1]

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that in addGuests.handler.ts lines 48-54, the authorization check allows access if `isTeamAdminOrOwner || isOrganizer || isAttendee`. The `isAttendee` check (line 52) grants any existing attendee the ability to add arbitrary guests to a booking. This is a security concern because attendees typically should not have authority to modify the organizer's event by adding third-party email addresses, which triggers calendar updates and emails. The finding correctly identifies that this permission model may be too permissive - an invitee can alter an organizer-owned event without explicit organizer authorization.
